events.ai_basis: Parts of the solution to this optimization problem in Section 3 were found with help from David Fox and Chat GPT-5.

events.credibility_reason: Scope ballooned from r ≤ 26 to all r within 12 days on a problem where a full proof would be a landmark; single author from outside the core field; the certificate artefact returned 404; the automated review's flagged imported-lemma hypothesis for r = 25, 26 has no recorded answer; Wikipedia and ProofAtlas still list it open. Only four weeks old, so lack of uptake is not yet decisive, hence doubtful rather than not_credible.

why: The statement is one universal inequality over all graphs, so every result restricted by chromatic number (r ≤ 24, r ≤ 26, r ≤ 29) or by vertex count (Fox–Pach–Suk) is a case. Pre-snapshot cases are journal-published, so digested. SoCG 2025 is a refereed proceedings, so digested. Sadhu v2 claims the whole statement but nobody has checked it. Its rapid scope growth, the dead artefact link and the unanswered (automated) objection make it doubtful, though it is too recent for not_credible. The Albertson–Berman papers are a different problem, so variant. AI: Fox–Pach–Suk arXiv credits Chat GPT-5 with finding parts of the solution to an optimisation the 1.64 constant depends on, which is mathematics in the result, so assisted. Sadhu v2 lists literature search, editing and verification assistance only, so none. Cao–Mehat name no system and say nothing about what the tools produced, so the record leaves systems empty and the answer is none.
doubts: Cao–Mehat declare generative AI was 'used substantially during the development of this work' without naming a system or saying what it produced; if it produced arguments, that event would be assisted. The Fox–Pach–Suk Chat GPT-5 credit is shared with a human and the size of its share is unstated; the call between assisted and none was close. The Oporowski–Zhao r = 6 attribution and its date rest on secondary sources.
